pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we shorten words like cannot to can’t?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts
2. use positive and negative statements in sentences

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts
   In simple words: practise until you can form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. use positive and negative statements in sentences
   In simple words: practise until you can use positive and negative statements in sentences. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes in the examples.
2. Explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes.
4. Show that you can: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Categorise sample sentences into negative or positive statements in small groups then display the work on a chart,
2. Make and display charts containing contracted forms of verbs,
3. Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced when the learner asks peers questions that elicit both positive and negative answer.
4. Digital Literacy: It is developed when the learner uses digital devices to search for online resources on contracted verbs. Values:
5. Unity: This is achieved as the learner interact collaboratively while asking each other questions.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts
2. use positive and negative statements in sentences

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
